output.brief: The August drop came from the failed chiller serving floors 6-8. It was out from 4 to 19 August and rooms ran 26-29 C. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1, and their overall score fell from 8.6 to 7.4. Scores for guests who checked out between 5 and 20 August were about 6.8, and they recovered after the repair. Floors 1-5 barely moved. Most negative comments (56) were about heat, and all of those came from floors 6-8. Cleanliness scores, inspection pass rates and kiosk metrics were flat, and the survey method did not change. So the evidence does not support blaming the housekeeping contractor or the kiosks, and I would not serve notice or pull the kiosks. The 6% rate rise may have nudged value scores a little. That dip is mostly seasonal, and I can't separate the two, so don't reverse the rate rise yet. Don't exclude the floor 6-8 responses from the score. That would hide a real failure. Next, reinstate the deferred maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spare parts on site, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. A further return-stay offer is optional, since every affected guest already got an apology and a half-night credit. I'm fairly confident, and I collected no extra evidence.
